newsitem.title: UK: Pavarotti bids for new million seller for Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Pavarotti bids for new million seller for Bosnia.

text.p: A new charity album in aid of Bosnia's war children by Italian operatic tenor Luciano Pavarotti looks set to top one million sales worldwide with its release in Britain next month.
Pavarotti joined forces with singer and actress Liza Minnelli and pop stars Elton John and Eric Clapton to record an open air concert this summer in his hometown of Modena.
It has now become an international recording hit and could top the 1.1 million sales achieved worldwide by his first Bosnia charity album last year.
"The UK will release the album on December 2 and this should bring the worldwide figure over one million," a spokeswoman for Decca Records said on Sunday.
The proceeds of both albums are going to the aid organisation War Child, started in 1991 by two cameramen shocked by what they saw in the war in Croatia.
The money is being used to set up a musical therapy centre for war-affected children in the Bosnian city of Mostar.

Pavarotti, hailing the release of the album in Britain, said: "The music centre in Mostar is rising from the ruins of war to make a haven for the children where they can join together and become strong."

"I was a child of war myself and at the end of the war we want more than anything else to come together to sing, hear and make music. In this way we can heal ourselves and feel we are truly alive again," he said in a statement.
Elton John wrote "Live like Horses" for Pavarotti, which the two sing as a duet.

The British pop star said: "He is hard to turn down ... I know how much it means to him because he's talked about it for a long time and I know what he's doing with the money and what he's achieving with it."
Some top rock and pop figures seemed in awe of Pavarotti and his booming voice in their shared duets at the Modena concert in June.
But the weighty tenor met his match in Liza Minnelli as they blasted out the classic "New York, New York" together.
Minnelli praised Pavarotti's handling of pop material. "It's very different and it's tough. There's all kinds of rhythmic pace that he's not used to.
"It's funny but it takes him a while to get it. But when he gets it, he nails it like nobody I've ever heard."
